title: The Future of Privacy and How to Stop it
description:
Privacy is essential to a free society, as the building block on which our fundamental rights stand, and strong privacy enhancing technologies are necessary to enable people to protect their rights in the face of an increasingly surveilled world. These technologies are increasingly getting targeted, with policymakers pushing for backdoors and other required weaknesses or mandated surveillance capabilities, and more recently threats to the people who write the code and provide the services that make privacy possible, not just the people who use it.

This talk will discuss why we need strong privacy and the tools that enable it, the threat landscape that we face as individuals and as builders, and how we can push back, both with building for resilient privacy enhancing technologies and by working together to create the legal and policy space necessary for a free society.
abstract: Privacy is a fundamental human right that enables our other fundamental rights. When society at large can't or won't stop the spread of ubiquitous surveillance, we need strong privacy technologies that return control and autonomy to users. Come learn about what’s at stake, understand the threats to privacy and supporting technologies, and how we can work to protect our right to build the tools we need,
